To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the airway inflammation in COPD is characterised by increased levels of C-reactive Protein (CRP).
the systemic inflammatory response in asthma and COPD is characterised by different cytokine profiles.

(1) the systemic inflammatory marker C-reactive protein (CRP) is increased in asthma and COPD and is associated with increased disease severity; (2) CRP is a marker of systemic inflammation in both asthma and COPD; (3) CRP is associated with disease progression in both diseases; (4) the increase of CRP is associated not only with the severity of the airway disease but also with the presence of systemic inflammation in other organs, such as the liver,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of C-Reactive Protein in airway diseases, predominantly Asthma and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
the pathophysiology of airway diseases and the identification of new biomarkers that can be used in the management of these patients.
the systemic face of airways diseases, with particular emphasis on the role of the acute phase protein C-reactive protein (CRP) as a biomarker and therapeutic target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
asthma and COPD represent different diseases, which are both characterised by an inflammatory component.
asthma is a disease of the airway wall, whereas COPD can be considered a disease of the whole respiratory system, in particular the lung.
asthma is characterised predominantly by a Th2-type response, whereas COPD shows a Th1-type response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the systemic inflammation in asthma is dominated by a Th2 cytokine pattern, with increased levels of IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, and in COPD a more complex pattern is observed, with a mixture of Th1- and Th2-type cytokines.
the systemic face of asthma is dominated by C-reactive protein (CRP) and that of COPD by interleukin-6.
C-reactive protein (CRP) is a systemic marker for airway inflammation in patients with COPD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the systemic inflammation in airway diseases, as reflected by C-reactive protein, is associated with the presence of airway inflammation.
the systemic inflammatory response is an important characteristic of both asthma and COPD.
the systemic inflammatory process is an important component of both asthma and COPD.
